title: First Spadolini government is formed.
text: The Spadolini I Cabinet, led by Giovanni Spadolini, was the 39th cabinet of the Italian Republic. The government, in office from 28 June 1981 to 23 August 1982, was led by for the first time in the republican history of Italy by a non-Christian Democrat Prime Minister, the Republican Spadolini.

title: 13-20 September – EuroBasket Women 1981 takes place in Senigallia.
text: Senigallia is a comune (municipality) and resort town on Italy's Adriatic coast. It is situated in the province of Ancona, in the Italian region of Marche, and lies approximately 30 kilometres north-west of the provincial capital city Ancona.

title: Primo Nebiolo is president of the International Association of Athletics Federations (until death in 1999).
text: Primo Nebiolo was an Italian sports official, best known as former president of the worldwide athletics federation IAAF and the FISU. Primo Nebiolo was the ideator of the IAAF Continental Cup.

title: “Anna dai capelli rossi （Anne of Green Gables）” by I Ragazzi dai Capelli Rossi
text: Anne of Green Gables is a Japanese animated television series and the fifth entry in Nippon Animation's World Masterpiece Theater franchise. It was adapted from the 1908 novel Anne of Green Gables by Lucy Maud Montgomery.

title: “Woman in Love”
text: "Woman in Love" is a song performed by Barbra Streisand and taken from her 1980 album Guilty. The song was written by Barry and Robin Gibb of the Bee Gees, who received the 1980 Ivor Novello award for Best Song Musically and Lyrically.

title: “Maledetta primavera”
text: "Maledetta primavera" is a song written by Paolo Cassella and Gaetano "Totò" Savio and performed by Italian singer Loretta Goggi in 1981, at the 31st edition of the Sanremo Music Festival. Coming second in the festival, it became a hit in Italy, with later covers in several other languages also garnering success around the world.

title: “Sarà perché ti amo”
text: "Sarà perché ti amo" is a song by Italian pop group Ricchi e Poveri, released in 1981 as the lead single from their ninth studio album, E penso a te. It became one of their biggest hits.

title: “Amoureux solitaires”
text: "Amoureux solitaires" is a song by the Belgian pop singer Lio. It was released in 1980 on Ariola and Arabella Records as the second single as well as the sixth track from her debut eponymous debut studio album.

title: “Enola Gay”
text: "Enola Gay" is an anti-war song by the English electronic band Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark, and the only single taken from their second studio album Organisation (1980). Written by lead vocalist and bassist Andy McCluskey, it addresses the atomic bombing of Hiroshima by the aircraft Enola Gay on 6 August 1945, toward the conclusion of World War II. title: “Out Here on My Own”
text: "Out Here on My Own" is a ballad from the 1980 musical film Fame, performed by Irene Cara and Frank Owens (piano). It was written by sibling songwriting duo Lesley Gore (lyricist) and Michael Gore (composer).

title: “Bette Davis Eyes”
text: "Bette Davis Eyes" is a song written and composed by Donna Weiss and Jackie DeShannon in 1974. It was recorded by DeShannon that year but made popular by Kim Carnes in 1981 when it spent nine non-consecutive weeks at the top of the U.S. Billboard Hot 100.
